findings.title: Team permission check uses AND instead of OR, so team admins are denied
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`. Since `isTeamAdmin` already matches ADMIN or OWNER roles and `isTeamOwner` matches only OWNER, the conjunction effectively requires the user to be the team OWNER. Team admins — who the variable name and the rest of the codebase say should be allowed — will get `FORBIDDEN`. It should be `||` (or just `isTeamAdmin`). Additionally, for personal bookings (`booking.eventType?.teamId` is null) this issues two pointless membership queries against `teamId = 0` on every call.

findings.title: EventManager is built from the session user's credentials, not the booking organizer's
findings.body: `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })` use the *caller's* credentials/destination calendar, but the handler explicitly allows team admins/owners and plain attendees to add guests. In those cases the calendar/video integration update (`eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`) runs with credentials that have no access to the organizer's calendar event, so the external calendar invite is silently not updated (or errors out) and the new guests never appear on the real event. The query at line 35-40 already fetches `booking.user.credentials` but never uses them; the organizer's credentials should be used instead.

findings.title: Emails are dispatched using the raw input list instead of the filtered guest list
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the unfiltered input, while only `uniqueGuests` were actually inserted. In `sendAddGuestsEmails` any attendee whose email appears in that list receives `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (a brand-new-booking confirmation). So re-submitting an email that already belongs to an existing attendee (or a blacklisted address that was filtered out) makes that existing attendee receive a duplicate 'your booking is confirmed' email instead of the 'guests added' notification. It should pass `uniqueGuests`, normalized the same way as the comparison.

findings.title: Blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive, allowing bypass and duplicate attendees
findings.body: `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lower-cased when parsed from the env var, but the incoming `guest` string is compared as-is (`!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`), so `Blocked@Example.com` passes a blacklist containing `blocked@example.com`. The same case-sensitivity applies to the existing-attendee comparison (`guest === attendee.email`), so the same person can be added again with different casing, creating duplicate attendee rows and duplicate emails. Both comparisons should normalize to lower case.

findings.title: No server-side deduplication or size limit on the guest list
findings.body: `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` only validates `z.array(z.string().email())` — no `.max()` and no uniqueness refinement (the uniqueness check exists only in the dialog component). The handler's filter removes guests already on the booking but never dedupes within the request, so a direct tRPC call with `["a@b.com", "a@b.com"]` inserts two identical attendee rows via `createMany`. With no upper bound, a single authenticated caller (including a mere attendee of the booking, per the permission check above) can insert thousands of attendees and trigger an email to each arbitrary address containing the booking details and meeting link — an email-amplification/abuse vector. Add a max length and dedupe server-side.

findings.title: findFirstOrThrow on `booking.userId || 0` yields an unhandled 500 for bookings without a user
findings.body: If `booking.userId` is null (possible for dynamic/managed or orphaned bookings), the lookup becomes `where: { id: 0 }` and `findFirstOrThrow` raises a Prisma `NotFoundError`, surfacing as an opaque INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR to the client instead of a meaningful tRPC error. Handle the null case explicitly (e.g. NOT_FOUND / BAD_REQUEST) rather than coercing to id 0.

findings.title: CalendarEvent is built without `team`, so team hosts never receive the guests-added email
findings.body: The `evt` object omits a `team` property (and `bookingId`/`eventTypeId`). In `sendAddGuestsEmails` the block `if (calendarEvent.team?.members) { ... OrganizerAddGuestsEmail({ teamMember }) }` is therefore dead code for this flow: for collective/round-robin team bookings only the single organizer is notified and the other hosts are not told that new guests were added, even though they are on the calendar event.

findings.title: Email failure is swallowed with a message that discards the error
findings.body: `catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` discards `err` entirely and uses `console.log` instead of the project's `logger`. When guest notification fails there is no stack trace, no error code and no booking id in the logs, making the failure undiagnosable in production. Log the error object (and ideally the booking id) via `@calcom/lib/logger`.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores the event type's disableStandardEmails settings
findings.body: Every other sender in this file takes an `eventTypeMetadata` argument and short-circuits on `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` / `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail`. `sendAddGuestsEmails` takes no metadata and sends unconditionally, so event types configured with `metadata.disableStandardEmails.all.host`/`.attendee` will still blast organizer and attendee emails when guests are added, violating the user's configuration.

findings.title: Subject line dereferences attendees[0] and can render an empty name
findings.body: `name: this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` throws a TypeError if the attendee list is empty, and newly added guests are created with `name: ""` in the handler, so if the ordering ever puts a new guest first the subject becomes `Guests Added: <eventType> with  at <date>`. Guard the access and fall back to the attendee email or organizer name.

findings.title: Validation error state is never reset, leaving a stale error on reopen
findings.body: `isInvalidEmail` is only cleared by the Cancel button. It is not reset in `onSuccess`, nor when the dialog is dismissed via Escape/overlay click (`onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}`), nor when the user edits the emails. As a result the red 'Emails must be unique and valid' message stays visible after a successful submit and reappears the next time the dialog is opened. Reset it when the dialog opens/closes and when `multiEmailValue` changes.

findings.title: Component inside packages/ui imports from its own package barrel, creating a cycle
findings.body: `import { Button, EmailField, Icon, Tooltip } from "@calcom/ui"` is a self-referential import: `packages/ui/index.tsx` now exports `MultiEmailLazy` → `MultiEmail` → `@calcom/ui`. Other components in this package import siblings relatively (e.g. `./components/form`). Such cycles can resolve to `undefined` components at module-evaluation time depending on bundler/SSR ordering. Use relative imports to the concrete modules instead.

findings.title: No tests for the new addGuests handler
findings.body: The PR adds a mutation that writes attendees to a booking, performs permission checks (organizer / team admin-owner / attendee), filters blacklisted and duplicate emails, updates external calendars and sends emails — with no unit or integration test. The permission expression bug (`&&` instead of `||`) and the raw-vs-filtered guest list bug would both have been caught by a basic handler test. Add tests covering: unauthorized caller rejected, team admin allowed, duplicate/blacklisted emails filtered, and the email payload containing only newly added guests.

findings.title: No guard for cancelled/past bookings or seated event types
findings.body: The handler accepts any `bookingId` regardless of `booking.status` or start time, so a direct call can append attendees to a CANCELLED/REJECTED booking and send them a CONFIRMED ICS REQUEST for an event that no longer exists. It also ignores `eventType.seatsPerTimeSlot`: attendees are inserted with `createMany` without any corresponding `BookingSeat` record, which bypasses seat accounting for seated event types. Reject non-accepted/past bookings and either reject or correctly handle seated events.
